intro: Each county's board of elections runs voting in that county. The State Board of Elections oversees them and sets the statewide rules.

elections.name: General election
elections.what: Federal, state, county, and local offices, plus any measures. Your exact ballot depends on where you live.

dates.label: Last day to register to vote
dates.detail: The deadline is 5 pm. If you miss it, you can still register and vote at the same time during early voting.

src.label: NC State Board of Elections: upcoming election

dates.label: Early voting
dates.detail: Vote in person at any early voting site in your county. Same-day registration is open at early voting sites. Early voting ends at 3 pm on Oct. 31. Each county sets its own sites and hours.

src.label: NC State Board of Elections: upcoming election
NC State Board of Elections: vote in person

dates.label: Mail ballot request deadline
dates.detail: Your request for an absentee ballot by mail is due by 5 pm. Military and overseas voters have different deadlines.

src.label: NC State Board of Elections: upcoming election

dates.label: Election Day
dates.detail: Polls are open 6:30 am to 7:30 pm. Vote at your assigned polling place. Mail ballots must be returned by 7:30 pm. Mail voters must include a copy of an acceptable photo ID or an ID Exception Form.

src.label: NC State Board of Elections: upcoming election

id_rule.text: You will be asked to show photo ID when you vote. Most voters use a driver's license. If you have no ID, you can still vote: fill out an ID Exception Form and vote a provisional ballot. Your county board of elections can give registered voters a free photo ID.
